title: Tesla Opens Robotaxi Service in Fort Worth, Its Seventh City
dek: Tesla started unsupervised Robotaxi rides in Fort Worth on Monday, a city that was not on its recent list of coming-soon markets. Four other cities named in October have not launched.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Electric cars plugged into public charging points

keyPoints: Tesla's Robotaxi account said on X that service in Fort Worth would start at 6 a.m. on November 2, with rides fully unsupervised.
The Fort Worth geofence covers about 143 square miles, according to Not a Tesla App; a separate estimate from Robotaxi Log put it near 104 square miles.
Fort Worth is Tesla's seventh unsupervised city, after Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando and Tampa, and it was not on the October list of coming-soon cities.
Las Vegas, Phoenix, Jacksonville and San Antonio, listed on October 21, have not launched.
body:
Tesla has added a seventh city to its unsupervised Robotaxi network. The company's Robotaxi account announced on X that service in Fort Worth, Texas, would begin at 6 a.m. on November 2, and rides were described as fully unsupervised, with no human safety monitor in the vehicle.

## A city that was not on the list

Electrek-style coverage has tended to track Tesla's stated next cities, but Fort Worth was not among them. On October 21, Tesla listed Las Vegas, Phoenix, Jacksonville and San Antonio as coming soon on its Robotaxi safety page, without dates. None of those four has launched. Electric Vehicles coverage noted that Fort Worth was not on the most recent list, and that it is Tesla's first new Robotaxi city since July.

## Size and scope

The launch zone is centered on downtown Fort Worth and reaches north toward Saginaw, west to White Settlement and south to Benbrook. Estimates of its size differ. Not a Tesla App put it at about 143 square miles, which would make it Tesla's third-largest unsupervised zone behind Austin and Houston. A tracing of the launch map by the Robotaxi Log site put it at about 104 square miles. Tesla has not said how many vehicles it assigned to the city.

The Fort Worth zone is not connected to Tesla's Dallas zone, because Arlington, Grand Prairie and Irving lie between them. Dallas is expected to receive Cybercab service later this month, according to Not a Tesla App, which would make it the second market after Austin to offer that vehicle.

## Pace against earlier targets

On Tesla's fourth-quarter call in January, Elon Musk said he expected fully autonomous vehicles in a quarter to a half of the United States by year-end and service in dozens of major cities. The network has not reached that scale. The Fort Worth launch adds one city in a month when Tesla's recent growth has mostly come from expanding existing zones, such as the roughly tenfold enlargement of Houston on October 26.

## What investors are watching

Tesla shares rose about 1% to $403.82 on November 2, according to Gotrade, while the Nasdaq Composite fell about 1%. Robotaxi expansion is a central part of the bull case for the stock, but the company has not disclosed vehicle counts or unit economics for the service, so the launch does not by itself change the revenue picture.

marketImpact.summary: A new unsupervised market supports the autonomy narrative around Tesla, but the company has not disclosed fleet size or economics for Fort Worth. The bigger test is whether the four coming-soon cities launch on schedule.
marketImpact.timeframe: Next 2-4 weeks, including the Dallas Cybercab launch and any new city announcements

tickers.rationale: Adds a seventh unsupervised Robotaxi city and reinforces the expansion story, though no fleet or revenue figures were disclosed
